key_insight: A deep-learning model using interictal intracranial EEG can identify epileptogenic zones across centers with performance comparable to published benchmarks and simple electrophysiology baselines.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could help improve pre-surgical localization of seizure-generating brain tissue in drug-resistant epilepsy.
method: Morlet wavelet temporal Transformer for multichannel interictal iEEG
Permutation-equivariant Set Attention spatial encoder to model long-range electrode interactions
Leave-one-center-out validation across seven independent centers
evidence_signal: Trained and tested on 50.5 hours of iEEG from 161 patients and 17,012 channels, the model achieved pooled AUROC 0.778 and performed above chance at all held-out centers.
watch_item: Results are promising but still depend on retrospective cross-center validation and an EZ definition tied to postoperative Engel Class I outcomes, so prospective clinical utility remains unproven.
paper_title: Localizing epileptogenic zones using interictal intracranial electroencephalography and deep learning
